intro: Earlysville is a rural community in Albemarle County, Virginia, north of Charlottesville and close to the Charlottesville-Albemarle Airport. In a mown field beside Earlysville Road stands a lone oak whose crown is far wider than it is tall, marked on OpenStreetMap as the Airport Oak. A reader sent us its photograph and puts it at about 450 years old. We do not know who owns the field, so the page suggests looking from the road.

trees.story:
A reader sent this oak as the Earlysville Oak, a white oak they put at about 450 years old, with a GPS fix taken in the field where it stands beside Earlysville Road, near the Charlottesville-Albemarle Airport in Virginia. On OpenStreetMap the same spot is marked as the Airport Oak.

The photograph shows the whole tree from across a mown field, and it is enormous. A short, broad trunk carries a crown that fills the sky, wider than it is tall, its lower limbs sweeping out almost level with the ground. The top of the crown has turned a deep red-brown while the lower branches are still green. Four people stand at the foot of the trunk and look small beside it, and two pickup trucks are parked under the edge of the crown.

The age is the reader's estimate, and we have no girth, height or register entry yet, so treat it as their figure. The leaves are too far off in the photograph to settle the species, so this page lists the tree as an oak and gives the reader's white oak beside it. If you have measured it, tell us here.

We do not know who owns the field. Look at the tree from the road.
